hindi: दण्ड-पारुष्य: स्पर्श करना, धमकाना, प्रहार करना।
english: Physical injury: touching, threatening, striking.
notes: Verbless list; the closing iti is not rendered. daṇḍa-pāruṣya = physical injury in the offences of Book 3 (glossary). avagūrṇa is taken as threatening (raising the hand or a weapon to strike); alternative: brandishing. prahata = striking, a blow.

words.gloss: vomit, urine, excrement, and the like

hindi: नाभि से नीचे के शरीर को हाथ, कीचड़, भस्म, धूल से छूने वाले का तीन पण का दण्ड; उन्हीं अपवित्रों से और पैर, थूक से छह पण; वमन, मूत्र, मल आदि से बारह पण।
english: For one touching the body below the navel with hand, mud, ash [or] dust, the penalty [is] three paṇas; with those same impure [things] and with foot [and] spittle, six paṇas; with vomit, urine, excrement and the like, twelve paṇas.
notes: The closing iti after the list of four substances is not rendered. "tair eva amedhyaiḥ" is taken as: with those same impure things (the mud, ash, dust just named); the referent is not stated. ṣṭhīvikā is taken as spittle (spelling printed pāda.ṣṭhīvikābhyāṃ, possibly for pāda-niṣṭhīvikābhyām; not flagged as a certain error). paṇa stays a unit name.

hindi: नाभि के ऊपर दुगुने, सिर पर चौगुने, समान लोगों में।
english: Above the navel double, on the head fourfold, among equals.
notes: The noun (the penalties, daṇḍāḥ) is not stated and is not supplied. sameṣu = among (persons of) equal rank, taken with the rule of unit 2.

words.gloss: carelessness, intoxication, delusion, and the like

hindi: श्रेष्ठों में दुगुने, हीनों में आधे दण्ड, दूसरों की स्त्रियों में दुगुने, प्रमाद, मद, मोह आदि से आधे दण्ड।
english: Among the superior double, among the inferior half penalties, among others' wives double, through carelessness, intoxication, delusion and the like half penalties.
notes: Verbless; read as an extension of units 2-3 (penalties depending on the rank of the person touched). viśiṣṭa = distinguished/superior; "श्रेष्ठ" is used for it in Hindi.

words.gloss: in seizing foot, garment, hand, hair

hindi: पैर, वस्त्र, हाथ, केश पकड़ने में छह पण से ऊपर के दण्ड।
english: In seizing by the foot, garment, hand [or] hair, penalties of six paṇas upward.
notes: ṣaṭ-paṇa-uttara taken literally as having six paṇas as the "higher/further" part, i.e. six paṇas upward. Alternatives: penalties increasing by six paṇas (each step); six paṇas as the lowest. avalambana = hanging on to, seizing.

words.gloss: in pressing, clasping, pulling, dragging, sitting upon

hindi: दबाने, लपेटने, खींचने, घसीटने, ऊपर बैठने में प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: In pressing, clasping, pulling, dragging [or] sitting upon, the first fine for rashness.
notes: añcana is taken as pulling (drawing); āveṣṭana as enclosing/clasping; adhyāsana as sitting on. Senses of the middle members are medium confidence.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. apa-√kram

hindi: गिराकर चले जाने वाले का आधा दण्ड।
english: For one who goes away after having caused [him] to fall, a half penalty.
notes: The object of pātayitvā is not stated; "[him]" is supplied in English only.

hindi: जिस अंग से शूद्र ब्राह्मण पर प्रहार करे, उसका वह कटवाए।
english: With whichever limb a śūdra strikes a brāhmaṇa, that [limb] of his [one] should have cut off.
notes: The subject of chedayet is not stated ("[one]"). The token asyac-chedayet is asya + chedayet (regular ch > cch after a short vowel; hyphen join in the e-text).

hindi: अवगूर्ण में निष्क्रय, स्पर्श में आधा दण्ड।
english: In threatening, redemption; in touching, a half penalty.
notes: Continues unit 8 (a śūdra and a brāhmaṇa). niṣkraya = redemption, i.e. buying oneself off; the exact form is not stated. avagūrṇa kept as in unit 1.

hindi: इससे चाण्डालों, अपवित्रों की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, the caṇḍālas and the impure are explained.
notes: Formula "tena X vyākhyātaḥ"; the verb is singular though two subjects (as glossary 4.4). aśuci = impure [persons]; who is meant is not stated.

words.gloss: having three paṇas as the lowest
having twelve paṇas as the highest

hindi: हाथ से धमकाने में तीन पण निम्नतम, बारह पण उच्चतम वाला दण्ड, पैर से दुगुना, दुःख उत्पन्न करने वाले द्रव्य से प्रथम साहस-दण्ड, प्राण को संकट में डालने वाले से मध्यम।
english: For threatening with the hand, the penalty [has] three paṇas as the lowest [and] twelve paṇas as the highest; with the foot, double; with an object causing pain, the first fine for rashness; with [one] endangering life, the middle.
notes: tri-paṇa-avara / dvādaśa-paṇa-para are paired as lower and upper limit; the glossary rendering of X-paṇa-avara as "X paṇas or lower" (4.10) does not fit this paired use, so the literal lowest/highest is given. madhyamaḥ is left bare (glossary 4.11); prāṇa-ābādhikena qualifies an unstated dravya.

words.gloss: of the articles wood, clod, stone, iron, stick, rope

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. ud-√pad

hindi: लकड़ी, ढेला, पत्थर, लोहा, डण्डा, रस्सी द्रव्यों में से किसी एक से बिना रक्त के दुःख उत्पन्न करने वाले का चौबीस पण का दण्ड, रक्त उत्पन्न करने में दुगुना, दूषित रक्त को छोड़कर।
english: For one causing pain without blood by any one of the articles wood, clod, stone, iron, stick [or] rope, the penalty [is] twenty-four paṇas; in causing blood, double; except [in the case of] bad blood.
notes: daṇḍa in the list of articles is a stick (the instrument), not the penalty. "śoṇita-utpādane" = in causing blood [to flow]. duṣṭa-śoṇita = bad (vitiated) blood; sense not further specified.

hindi: मृत के समान, रक्तहीन रूप से मारने वाले का, या हाथ-पैर का पारञ्चिक करने वाले का प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; हाथ, पैर, दाँत के तोड़ने में, कान, नाक के काटने में और घाव के फाड़ने में, दूषित घावों को छोड़कर।
english: For one who strikes [a man] bloodlessly, like one dead, or who makes a pārañcika of hand and foot, the first fine for rashness; and in breaking a hand, foot [or] tooth, in cutting off an ear [or] nose, in splitting open a wound; except [in the case of] bad wounds.

text_flags.why: stray extra c (vidāraṇe cca); the line has only one conjunction ca

notes: pārañcika is obscure and kept untranslated (possibly an injury or disabling of hand and foot); the compound hasta-pāda-pārañcika is read as tat-puruṣa. The object of ghnataḥ is not stated ("[a man]"). mṛta-kalpa = resembling dead. The last clause continues the list: "and in ... splitting open a wound".

words.gloss: in obstructions of speech, movement, eating

hindi: जाँघ, गर्दन तोड़ने में या आँख फोड़ने में, और वाणी, चेष्टा, भोजन के अवरोध में मध्यम साहस-दण्ड और उठ खड़े होने का व्यय।
english: In breaking the thigh [or] neck, or in splitting the eye, and in obstructing speech, movement [or] eating, the middle fine for rashness and the expense of rising up.
notes: samutthāna-vyaya = expense of rising up (the sense "recovery" only in notes, glossary 4.11).

hindi: विपत्ति होने पर कण्टकशोधन के लिए ले जाया जाए।
english: In misfortune [he] should be led to the cleansing of thorns.
notes: vipatti = misfortune, ruin; the likely sense is the death of the victim, but the text does not say so. The subject of nīyeta is not stated ("[he]"). kaṇṭaka-śodhana kept literal (glossary 4.1).

hindi: बड़े जनसमूह के एक को मारने पर प्रत्येक का दुगुना दण्ड।
english: Of a great crowd striking one, for each a double penalty.
notes: Read as: when a great crowd strikes one [person], each of them is liable to a double penalty. mahā-jana kept literal (a great number of people). Note the token mahā.janasya-ekaṃ is a hyphen join of two words.

hindi: “बासी कलह या अनुप्रवेश पर अभियोग नहीं चलाया जाना चाहिए,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "A stale quarrel or an entering-in is not to be prosecuted," say the teachers.
notes: anupraveśa is obscure and kept literal ("entering in"); possible senses: intrusion, or joining in a quarrel already begun. paryuṣita = stale (that has passed the night), i.e. an old quarrel. The closing iti is carried by the quotation marks (glossary 3.5).

hindi: “अपराधी की मुक्ति नहीं है,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "There is no release for an offender," says Kautilya.

text_flags.why: the quotation closed by iti has no opening quotation mark in the e-text (units 17 and 19 have both marks)

notes: Closing iti carried by quotation marks only; the opening mark is supplied in the translation and flagged.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. a-√kṣam

hindi: “कलह में पहले आया हुआ जीतता है, क्योंकि सहन न करने वाला आगे दौड़ पड़ता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: "In a quarrel the one who came first wins, for the one who does not endure rushes forward," say the teachers.
notes: pūrva-āgata may mean one who came first (to the court, or to the scene); the text does not say which.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: "No," says Kautilya.

hindi: पहले या बाद में पहुँचे हुए के साक्षी प्रमाण; साक्षी न होने पर प्रहार या कलह का संकेत।
english: Of one who has approached first or afterwards, the witnesses [are] the authority; when there are no witnesses, the blow or the indication of the quarrel [is].
notes: abhigata (approached) is ambiguous: approached the court/the officer, or approached the other party; the order "first or later" is taken with it. upaliṅgana = indication, mark (obscure; kept literal). ghāta here = blow (not "killing" of glossary 4.7). Predicates are supplied only as bare copulas in brackets in English.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. a-prati-√brū

hindi: प्रहार के अभियोग का उत्तर न देने वाले का उसी दिन पश्चात्कार।
english: Of one not replying to the charge of a blow, on that very day, the paścāt-kāra (literally "making-behind").
notes: paścāt-kāra is obscure and kept untranslated; literally "making behind / putting behind", perhaps being put in the wrong or defeated, but the text does not say.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. apa-√hṛ

words.gloss: in damaging garment, ornament, money, gold, wares

hindi: कलह में द्रव्य का अपहरण करने वाले का दस पण का दण्ड; छोटे द्रव्य की क्षति में वह और उतना दण्ड; मोटे द्रव्य की क्षति में वह और दुगुना दण्ड; वस्त्र, आभरण, धन, सोना, माल की क्षति में वह और प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: In a quarrel, for one carrying off an article, a penalty of ten paṇas; in damaging a petty article, that and that much as penalty; in damaging a coarse article, that and a double penalty; in damaging a garment, ornament, money, gold [or] wares, that and the first fine for rashness.
notes: tat ("that") is not defined; it probably refers to the article or its value, but the text does not say. hiṃsā = injury, damage (to articles). sthūlaka kept literal "coarse" (doubt, glossary 4.1). hiraṇya = money (gold only in notes), suvarṇa = gold, bhāṇḍa = wares (glossary 5.2, 4.6); bhāṇḍa could also be vessels.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √kṣubh

hindi: दूसरे की दीवार को प्रहार से हिला देने वाले का तीन पण का दण्ड; काटने, तोड़ने में छह पण, और प्रतिकार।
english: For one shaking another's wall by striking, a penalty of three paṇas; in cutting [and] splitting, six paṇas; and the remedy.
notes: pratīkāra = remedy (glossary 14.4), probably repair of the damage; not stated. chedana-bhedane is a dual locative.

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. pra-√kṣip

hindi: दूसरे के घर में दुःख उत्पन्न करने वाला द्रव्य फेंकने वाले का बारह पण का दण्ड; प्राण को संकट में डालने वाले का प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: For one throwing into another's house an article causing pain, a penalty of twelve paṇas; [an article] endangering life, the first fine for rashness.
notes: prāṇa-ābādhikam is taken as an elided dravyam (the article), bracketed in English.

hindi: छोटे पशुओं को लकड़ी आदि से दुःख देने में एक पण या दुगुना दण्ड; रक्त उत्पन्न करने में दुगुना।
english: In causing pain to small animals with wood and the like, a penalty of a paṇa or double [that]; in causing blood, double.
notes: "paṇo dvi.guṇo vā" read as a paṇa or double (that). "Causing blood" = causing blood to flow.

hindi: बड़े पशुओं के इन्हीं स्थानों में दुगुना दण्ड और उठ खड़े होने का व्यय।
english: For large animals, in just these cases, a double penalty and the expense of rising up.
notes: sthāna (place/instance) is read as the cases of unit 26 (pain with wood and the like, causing blood). Printed sthāneṣv dvi- is regular sandhi.

words.gloss: of trees of town and park

hindi: नगर, उपवन के पुष्प, फल, छाया वाले वृक्षों के अंकुर काटने में छह पण, छोटी शाखा काटने में बारह पण, मोटी शाखा काटने में चौबीस पण, तने के वध में प्रथम साहस-दण्ड, समुच्छेद में मध्यम।
english: Of trees of town [and] park that have flowers, fruit [and] shade: in cutting a shoot, six paṇas; in cutting a small branch, twelve paṇas; in cutting a stout branch, twenty-four paṇas; in destroying the trunk, the first fine for rashness; in cutting off entirely, the middle.

text_flags.why: extra c: ccch; śākhā + chedane gives śākhāc.chedane, as in the preceding kṣudra.śākhāc.chedane

notes: Compound pura-upavana-vanaspatīnām read as trees of town and park (alternative: trees of town-parks). vadha of the trunk = destruction (glossary 4.10 style). samucchitti = cutting off entirely, uprooting. Printed forms with c.ch (phalac.chāyāvatāṃ, prarohac.chedane, śākhāc.chedane) are regular sandhi. Unit 12 prints caturviṃśati without the dot, here catur.viṃśati; both read the same.

words.gloss: in shrubs and creepers having flowers, fruit, shade
in trees of holy places, penance groves, cremation grounds

hindi: पुष्प, फल, छाया वाली झाड़ियों, लताओं में आधे दण्ड, और पुण्य स्थानों, तपोवनों, श्मशानों के वृक्षों में।
english: In shrubs [and] creepers having flowers, fruit [and] shade, half penalties; and in the trees of holy places, penance groves [and] cremation grounds.
notes: Reading: "puṣpa-phala-chāyāvat" qualifies both gulma and latā. The final compound is read as trees of holy places, of penance groves and of cremation grounds.

hindi: सीमा के वृक्षों, चैत्यों और चिह्नित वृक्षों में तथा राज-वनों में वे ही दण्ड दुगुने किए जाएँ।
english: In boundary trees, in caityas and in marked trees, and in the king's forests, those very penalties are to be made double.
notes: caitya kept untranslated (glossary 5.2); it may be a tree or a sacred object, the text does not say. "those very penalties" refers to the penalties of units 28-29. ālakṣita = marked/noticeable (trees).
